title: Linux launch adapter (POSIX sh, exec bit, shebang normalisation)
question_or_target: Implement release/platforms/linux launch logic and prove the shipped shell scripts actually run under real Linux bash — where CRLF line endings are rejected outright, unlike Git Bash which tolerates them.

implementation.crlf_policy: CR byte => named ERROR:CRLF_REJECTED; no silent dos2unix
implementation.shebang: normalize to #!/usr/bin/env bash on an LF working copy
implementation.exec_bit: chmod +x on normalize dest; launch does not rely on +x

evidence.claim: bash -n under real GNU bash on Linux (python uname AND bash uname agree; bash --version is GNU, not MSYS/MinGW) passes every shipped LF script.
Each shipped script executed with a trivial argument via the adapter (explicit bash, not shebang) exits 0 with the expected stdout prefix.
A deliberately CRLF-converted copy of longrun.sh fails bash -n, adapter check (ERROR:CRLF_REJECTED), and shebang-exec; the LF original stays green in the same run.
